newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids steady amid talk of emerging demand.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids steady amid talk of emerging demand.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices held steady Tuesday amid talks of emerging demand to replenish inventory from utilities on the East Coast.
"There're more requirements than expected," noted one physical trader, referring to reports of higher-than-expected amount of resid nominated for April by some utilities.
Traffic restriction on the Mississippi River after a barged capsized a week ago kept spot resid supplies from reaching most users in the Gulf and Midwest, traders said.
"You still have some tremendous problems with transportation," said one Midwest trader.
In the Gulf, three percent sulphur grade was stable at $14.25-14.50 a barrel. Three percent paper slipped to $13.80-14.00 from $13.85-14.20 Monday. One percent physical stayed at $14.88.
NYH one percent physical was firm at $16.00-25 with offers as high as $16.50. One percent NYH paper for April edged down to $15.60-80 from Monday's $15.90-16.10.
NYH HSFO grades were mostly unchanged but 2.2 percent firmied 25 cents to $14.00-25 on reported buying interest from one New England utility.
The NYMEX May crude contract settled down seven cents to $20.99 a bbl after losing 79 cents the past two sessions.
At the New York City gate, day-ahead natural gas rebounded today in line with higher prices in the Gulf on expectation of demand to refill underground storage after the winter season.
Swing gas deliveries at New York City gate rose to $2.15-2.20 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) or $13.61 a barrel equivalent from Monday's $2.10-2.15/mmBtu or $13.14 a barrel equivalent.
Natgas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, edged up to $1.84/mmBtu or $11.59/bbl equivalent from yesterday's $1.80/mmBtu or $11.34/bbl equivalent.
